commit.message:

session, runner and attempt lifecycle. Command controls are offered only
when the child's command controller manages the long-open bash call,

commit.message:
test: wait for a cancelled command's process before removing its cwd (#2902)

On Windows, Pi ends a cancelled bash command with a taskkill it does not
await, and its tool call returns once the shell exits. The command-action
test removed the command's cwd while its process could still be alive.
The command now records its pid and teardown waits for that process to
exit. The supervisor-owner test's cleanup retries like the other
Windows-safe cleanups; nothing in its process holds that directory.

Related to #2901

commit.message:
fix: let forked subagents reuse the parent's prompt cache (#2879)

* fix: let forked subagents reuse the parent's prompt cache

A forked child now sends its parent's system prompt, tool declarations and
inherited messages unchanged (signed Anthropic thinking included), and gets
its own agent prompt, boundary and tool list in a <subagent_instructions>
block of its task message. On Anthropic-style endpoints with session
affinity it names the parent session so routers keep it on the parent's
cache. Fresh children are unchanged.

* fix: declare a fork child's own definition of a parent tool and scope its session affinity to the parent's model

A fork kept the parent's declaration whenever a tool name matched, so a
child with its own structured_output schema was shown the parent's schema
while its tool checked its own. A differing definition is now declared
again at the fork point, as Pi records a changed tool. The parent's
session id is sent as the session-affinity header only when the child
runs on the model that wrote its inherited history. Docs state the fork
prompt contract, and the changelog credits @gabsn.

* docs: say a redefined parent tool misses the cache on every model

* docs: keep the agents frontmatter reference within the guide limit

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: retry result cleanup silently while a runner holds the run lease (#2897)

The result watcher acknowledged a mission observer and retired a delivered
result with the generic 200 ms blocking lease wait, so a runner still
publishing the same run parked the host event loop and logged a stack trace
before the existing 100 ms retry succeeded. Cleanup now makes one lease
attempt and retries a busy lease without logging.

commit.message:
fix: keep a supervisor ask alive while its notice waits behind a busy parent (#2900)

* fix: keep a supervisor ask alive while its notice waits behind a busy parent run

The child's contact_supervisor wait counted from when it wrote the request, but Pi
holds the parent's request notice until the parent's current tool call returns. A
long parent tool call therefore expired asks before the parent model saw them.

While parentWake reports the notice as queued, the parent's existing channel poll
moves the request file's expiresAt forward (renewing at half the ask timeout), and
the child re-reads expiresAt on each poll. The extension stops when the notice's
message_start reaches extensions, or when the parent run settles with it undelivered.

Related to #2894

* fix: keep a renewed supervisor request file private

* fix: report a failed supervisor request renewal once

commit.message:
fix: pin tool descriptions without the note a host appends (#2899)

With Pi's codemode on, Pi appends a script-call note to each declared
script-callable tool and records that decorated description. Declaration
pinning re-registered the recorded description, Pi decorated it again,
and bg_wait gained one more note and was re-declared on every session
start. Pinning now compares and reuses the recorded description without
a repeated trailing paragraph or a paragraph appended after the current
description.

Related to #2889

launching Pi process was gone never gets observed proof either, so its
slot stayed counted for the session. Workflow children in any terminal
state now qualify under the same dead-PID, namespace and staleness
evidence; top-level runner slots stay failed-only.

commit.message:
fix: read tool results from the toolResult messages Pi emits (#2871)

* fix: read tool results from the toolResult messages Pi emits

Pi delivers every tool result, including a call blocked by a tool_call
handler, as tool_execution_end followed by a toolResult message_end; it
never emits tool_result_end. The foreground tool-budget block, recent tool
output and mutating-failure attention, and the background runner's live
budget status, all waited for tool_result_end, so none of them ran. They
now run on the toolResult message, and the tool_result_end branches in the
run files are removed. Test fixtures emit Pi's real event sequence.

Related to #2846

* fix: match parallel tool results to their call by toolCallId

Pi runs tool calls in parallel by default, emitting every
tool_execution_start before the first toolResult message, so the single
last-started snapshot recorded a failed call against another call's path
and left later results with no snapshot. The foreground executor and the
background runner now key pending snapshots by toolCallId and keep the
last-started slot only for events without one.

Related to #2846

* fix: size per-call tool snapshots with expanded dynamic groups; use the strict block check for live status

Related to #2846

fix: read tool results from the toolResult messages Pi emits (#2871)

* fix: read tool results from the toolResult messages Pi emits

Pi delivers every tool result, including a call blocked by a tool_call
handler, as tool_execution_end followed by a toolResult message_end; it
never emits tool_result_end. The foreground tool-budget block, recent tool
output and mutating-failure attention, and the background runner's live
budget status, all waited for tool_result_end, so none of them ran. They
now run on the toolResult message, and the tool_result_end branches in the
run files are removed. Test fixtures emit Pi's real event sequence.

Related to #2846

* fix: match parallel tool results to their call by toolCallId

Pi runs tool calls in parallel by default, emitting every
tool_execution_start before the first toolResult message, so the single
last-started snapshot recorded a failed call against another call's path
and left later results with no snapshot. The foreground executor and the
background runner now key pending snapshots by toolCallId and keep the
last-started slot only for events without one.

Related to #2846

* fix: size per-call tool snapshots with expanded dynamic groups; use the strict block check for live status

Related to #2846

commit.message:
fix: release a workflow's capacity slot when an async child fails to launch (#2858)

The workflow host records an async child's run id in its roster before the
launch runs. When the launch then fails before any runner exists (an unknown
model, a runner that cannot start), the child's run directory gets no
status.json, so its process evidence stayed unknown and the terminal
workflow's active-capacity slot was retained for as long as the session lived.

A failed roster step with an error whose run directory has no status,
process-terminal or runner-startup file now counts as having no process,
like a synchronous child. The check runs only where evidence was already
unknown, so the common path does no extra filesystem work.

Fixes #2856

commit.message:
test: stop the schedule history race test from racing the lease wait (#2867)

The contender waited for the owner's history lease with the lease's own
200 ms deadline, while the owner held that lease across the test's IPC
round trip and 5 ms file polling. On a slow Windows runner that took
longer, so the contender's schedule.run timed out (an error the fixture
ignored) and its history entry was missing.

The contender now waits for the test to signal that the owner exited
before taking the lease, after first observing it held, and the fixture
fails when schedule.run returns an error.

Related to #2862

fix(slash): let hosts that render ctx.ui.custom over RPC pass the component gate (#2849)

* fix(slash): let hosts that render ctx.ui.custom over RPC pass the component gate

0.77.0 replaced the component probes with `ctx.mode !== "tui"`, which is right for
stock Pi RPC where custom() is a no-op stub, but it also blocks hosts that implement
the custom-UI contract themselves and still bind as mode "rpc" (pi-web does).

Distinguish the stub by arity: stock Pi defines custom() with no parameters
(core/extensions/runner.js, modes/rpc/rpc-mode.js), while a real implementation takes
(factory, options).

* fix: gate component screens over RPC on an explicit host opt-in

Function arity is an implicit probe: a future stock stub that names its
parameters would bring back the silent no-op screens of #2766. A host that
renders ctx.ui.custom() over RPC now sets PI_SUBAGENTS_COMPONENT_UI=1.

commit.message:
feat: let a forked subagent reuse its parent's prompt cache (#2857)

* feat: keep the parent's tool declarations in a forked child's requests

A forked child starts with its parent's history, whose system messages declare the
parent's tools, and its own first system message removes the tools it may not use.
Providers cache the tool list before everything else, so every request of a fork
missed the parent's prompt cache.

A fork's runtime now handles context_with_system: the child's own system messages,
those written since the fork's session header, lose their removals of inherited
tools, so parent-era messages are sent unchanged. When a context handler changed
the conversation, Pi sends one leading system message instead; its tools are set
to the inherited ones in order, then the child's own. The inherited declarations
come from the session once per fork.

The child still does not register the tools it may not use, so a call to one gets
Pi's "Tool <name> not found" error and runs nothing. The session file keeps Pi's
own record of the child's tools; only what a request sends changes.

* feat: send a forked child's inherited history as the parent sent it

A forked child's context handler removed the parent's subagent calls, their results
and parent-only notices from the history it inherited. Every fork has at least one
such call, the one that launched it, so its requests diverged from the parent's
there, and any change made Pi collapse all system messages into one merged head. A
provider that keeps the parent's system prompt and sends later changes separately
then got a different prompt and missed the parent's whole prompt cache.

In a fork, messages older than the fork's session header now pass unchanged apart
from tool-id sanitizing, which changes nothing when the parent's provider already
accepted the ids. Messages the child adds keep today's filtering, and children that
are not forks are unchanged. The child still cannot run subagent: it stays
unregistered outside fanout, so a call gets Pi's not-found error.

* fix: stop declaring a fork's parent tools once compaction removed the inherited history

A fork child cached its parent's tool list once per session and kept declaring it after a compaction dropped every inherited message from the request. With no parent prefix left to match, those tools only cost tokens and could never run. The parent's tools are now kept only while the request still holds a message older than the fork.

* fix: say only a child's own context is filtered, not a fork's inherited history

* feat: declare contact_supervisor alongside subagent so a fork's tools match its parent's

A forked child declared contact_supervisor, which its parent never had, so even with the
parent's other tools kept its tool list differed and its first request missed the parent's
prompt cache.

A session that has subagent now also declares contact_supervisor, with the definition
children use: both registrations share one declaration. It is toggled with subagent by tool
activation and active from the start in eager mode. Called in a session that is not a
subagent it returns an error saying the session has no supervisor. A child keeps its working
tool: foreground children load no ambient extensions, and the background runner sets
PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD, so the parent extension registers nothing there.

The CHANGELOG entry covers the whole branch.

commit.message:
fix: give a workflow resume of an outside run its own report path (#2842)

* fix: give a workflow resume of an outside run its own report path

An output-less workflow resume was moved off the resumed run's recorded output only when an earlier child of the same workflow had claimed it, so resuming a run from outside the workflow wrote over that run's report. The resumed run now always owns the report it saved: an output-less resume of a run with a recorded output gets the key's default output path. The claim for the resumed path and the absolute-path-only foreground check are no longer needed and are removed.

Related to #2839

* fix: keep a resumed run's report when the workflow default names the same file

* docs: say a resumed workflow report can get the run id suffix

* test: pin the resumed run's own report path instead of the overwrite

An explicit output still wins; workflow resumes keep their output-claim routing.

commit.message:
fix: show a timed-out background child's partial output in its notice (#2830)

* fix: show a timed-out background child's partial output in its notice

A timed-out background run's summary was only the timeout line, so the completion notice and status dropped the child's partial output and its file path. The summary now keeps a child's partial output after the timeout line, and the existing cap adds the preview and path. Fixes #2829.

* fix: cap a timed-out child's partial output when its recovery summary follows it

A timed-out child's published output is its partial text plus a recovery summary, but the output artifact holds only the partial text, so capInlineOutput found no file containing the whole output and inlined all of it. Cap the longest head the file holds, ending before one of the last few blank-line blocks, and keep the unfiled trailing blocks inline after the Full output line.

---------

commit.message:
fix: run workflows that call Promise.all when the host freezes Promise (#2828)

* fix: run workflows when the host freezes Promise statics

Pi-Bolt freezes built-ins in every realm, so Promise.all and its siblings
are non-writable and non-configurable. A Proxy over Promise must return
the original value for such properties, so the workflow sandbox's wrapped
Promise.all threw a TypeError. The sandbox Promise now proxies a plain
constructor that shares Promise.prototype.

* docs: link the changelog entry to its PR

commit.message:
fix: resume after manual compaction through the prompt lifecycle (#2812)

* fix: resume after manual compaction through a prompt, once the parent is idle

After a manual /compact with background subagents running, the resume run went out without the prompt sections extensions set in before_agent_start, so the provider re-read the conversation without its prompt cache. Pi emits session_compact before it clears its compaction state, so the parent still counted as busy and parentWake forwarded the resume as a triggerTurn sendMessage, which starts the run without before_agent_start (earendil-works/pi#5581). Calling sendUserMessage from the hook is not an option either: prompt() rejects while compaction is in progress.

The resume now polls every 50 ms for up to 10 s until the parent is idle, then goes through parentWake's prompt path. It is dropped if another run starts first, the session changes or shuts down, or no async work is still active.

* test: keep the parent busy through a poll before asserting no compaction resume

The busy-parent assertion ran before the first 50 ms poll fired, so it passed even with the idle check removed. Also credits #2812 in the changelog entry.

commit.message: chore(release): v0.77.0

fix(schedules): release a schedule's claim when its async run is dead (#2810)

* fix(schedules): release a schedule's claim when its async run is dead

A scheduled run whose async runner died before writing a terminal status
kept the schedule's activeRunId and active.lock, so every later fire was
recorded as skipped_overlap and a session restore did not recover it.

A fire that overlaps an active run, and restoreOne, now reconcile that
run with the existing stale-run reconciler (dead runner PID, or no status
update for 24h). A terminal result releases the claim through finishRun;
on the fire path the due occurrence then launches, advancing the trigger
once. A live run is still skipped, and a relaunching fire removes the lock
only while it still names the dead run.

Fixes #2806

Co-authored-by: Kevin Blackburn-Matzen <matzen@adobe.com>

* fix(schedules): keep the due fire and a newer claim when releasing a dead run

Restoring a schedule whose active run was dead released it through the
completion path, which recorded the overdue occurrence as skipped and
advanced the trigger, so a restart after a host crash lost that fire even
with catchUp "latest". Restore now releases the claim without consuming
the occurrence and applies the normal restore policy to the latest record.

Two sessions firing the same occurrence could both release the dead run;
the slower one wrote its stale snapshot over the other's new claim. The
release now re-reads the schedule and acts only while it still names the
dead run; otherwise the fire skips as a lost claim without writing the
schedule.

Co-authored-by: Kevin Blackburn-Matzen <matzen@adobe.com>

* fix(schedules): re-arm a restored schedule when recording its released run fails

restoreOne released a dead run's claim and then re-entered the restore
policy. If writing the run record or history.json threw, the release had
already cleared the claim but the re-entry never ran, so the schedule had
no timer for the rest of the session. The re-entry now runs in a finally
block on the latest record, and the original error still propagates.

Co-authored-by: Kevin Blackburn-Matzen <matzen@adobe.com>

* fix(schedules): release a restored dead claim once without re-entering restore

When finishRun's schedule write failed during a restore, the finally block
re-read the still-claimed record and re-entered restoreOne, which failed
again and recursed until a RangeError replaced the filesystem error.

Restore now releases a dead or terminal claim at most once and never
re-enters itself. On success it continues to the existing policy with the
latest record; on failure it arms the schedule from disk so the next fire
retries the release, and the original error propagates unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Kevin Blackburn-Matzen <matzen@adobe.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Kevin Blackburn-Matzen <matzen@adobe.com>

commit.message:
fix: read no project settings during discovery when the session declined project trust (#2805)

* fix: read no project settings during discovery when the session declined project trust

Discovery built the project source tree before applying trust, and resolving the project root parses .pi/settings.json strictly. A malformed or invalid file therefore broke untrusted user-scope discovery and preflight, and project agentExcludeDirs could hide user agents. Untrusted lookups now build their own cached source tree with no project root, directories, settings or root/project package entries; trusted lookups are unchanged.

Related to #2804

* fix: apply runtime agent settings from the same untrusted view

Review follow-up: applyRuntimeAgentSettings still built a trusted source tree, so a malformed project settings file broke untrusted launches when an extension had registered a runtime agent. Related to #2804

commit.message:
fix: ignore project subagent settings, agents and packages when the session declined project trust (#2803)

Discovery and public preflight take projectTrusted (default true). With false, the default scope projects as user, an explicit project scope is rejected, and project settings, agents, chains, and project or root package.json entries are dropped. The executor binds discovery to ctx.isProjectTrusted() once per execute call, so foreground, async, workflow, resume, append-step and validation lookups follow the session, and an explicit project scope returns a tool error. Runtime agents take model settings from the scope discovery used, and advertised agents follow the session's trust.

Related to #2764

The executor binds discovery to ctx.isProjectTrusted() once per execute call, so foreground, async, workflow, resume, append-step and validation lookups follow the session, and an explicit project scope returns a tool error. Runtime agents take model settings from the scope discovery used, and advertised agents follow the session's trust.

commit.message:
fix: resolve runtime extension siblings from disk, not the caller's extension (#2761)

* fix: resolve runtime extension siblings from disk, not the caller's extension

pi-subagents injects a few runtime extensions into every child session and
derives their paths from the running module's own extension:

  `subagent-prompt-runtime${path.extname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))}`

That assumes the running module and its siblings are always published with the
same extension (a source checkout uses .ts, the npm package ships compiled .js)
and never change during the lifetime of the process. When an installed package
is replaced in place — for example an npm/Pi update moving a .ts-source install
to the compiled .js layout — a long-running host keeps handing children a .ts
path that no longer exists, and every subagent spawn fails with:

  Failed to load extension "…/subagent-prompt-runtime.ts": Extension path does not exist

Resolve the sibling from what is actually on disk, at the moment the child
launch is built (per launch, not once at module load), so the compiled .js is
used when present while a source checkout keeps using .ts. Apply the same rule
to the async runner bootstrap and the binary bootstrap, and let
isSubagentRuntimeExtensionPath() recognise either extension.

* docs: changelog entry for runtime sibling path resolution

Credits @barjatiyasaurabh and @gitwyy.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

commit.message:
perf: cap child output inlined into parent results (#2779)

* perf: cap child output inlined into parent results

Async completion notices, completed-run status and foreground results show the first 2,000 characters of a longer child output, then the path, size and line count of the retention-managed artifact that holds all of it. Output with no readable artifact containing it stays whole. Workflow child previews drop from 4 KB to 2,000 bytes, status structured-output previews drop to 500 characters when a path line follows, failed children that produced output get an Error: line, and the launch receipt guidance is two short lines.

Related to #2774

* fix: cap inline output that also names an explicit output file

A child with an explicit output file and inline output mode returns its text followed by an "Output saved to:" line. The retention artifact holds only the text, so the check that the artifact contains the inline output failed and foreground results, async notices and completed status kept the whole report. commit.message:
feat(tui): show subagent messages as Pi's own message block (#2753)

* feat(tui): show subagent messages as Pi's own message block

Each message pi-subagents put in the main chat had its own look:
bordered cards for supervisor requests, replies and attention notices,
glyph lines for completions, colored lines for steering, and Pi's
default block with raw type labels for reminders and wakes.

Every one now renders as the block Pi draws for [skill] and
[compaction]: a single [subagent] line whose label color names the kind
and whose status word takes the theme's status color. A click opens one
block and Pi's expand key opens all of them, showing the text the main
agent read as markdown. One registry in src/tui/subagent-messages.ts
owns the headline and body of every message and entry type.

Completion and workflow child notices carry render-only details, which
Pi never sends to the model; notices saved earlier are read from their
text. The text the model reads is unchanged.

* docs: credit #2753 in the changelog

* test: render the watchdog warning through the shared message renderer

The watchdog no longer registers its own renderer; the subagent message registry owns every message type, so the slash-command test renders the blocker message through it.

* feat(tui): keep Pi's expand hint on collapsed subagent messages

A collapsed [subagent] line ends with the same dim (ctrl+o to expand) hint Pi's [skill] line shows, or (click to expand) when no key is bound to Pi's expand action.

* fix(tui): keep watchdog stalemate, stale and failed-review state on the collapsed line

Collapsed watchdog warnings showed only the severity, so a stalemate that stopped the run looked like any other blocker. The headline now adds the same state labels the expanded text uses, except the routine displayed state.

commit.message:
fix: write result indexes before the result becomes readable (#2743)

A workflow awaiting an async child could read the child's pending result before the child had written its index entries, clean up, and return. The child then wrote the index entries, which nobody removed. Write the payload to its temporary file, then the indexes, then rename the payload into place, so a consumer that can see the payload always finds and removes every index. A failed index write still publishes the payload before the error is rethrown, so it stays recoverable.

Because a valid index can now briefly precede its payload, a run-id lookup no longer deletes an index whose payload it cannot find yet; the age-based sweep in cleanupResultIndexes owns payload-less indexes.

Related to #2741

commit.message:
feat(inspector): bundle a tmux inspector plugin (#2719)

* feat(inspector): bundle a tmux inspector plugin

Fleet's Enter/H previously had no bundled path for tmux users - the most
common multiplexer for this tool - leaving them with 'no inspector plugin
available' unless they installed Herdr.

Adds a built-in tmux plugin alongside herdr and ghostty:

- available when TMUX is set (not on win32); open splits the focused
  window and runs the standard read-only inspector command in the new
  pane, so regular tmux keys (including the prefix) keep working
- writes a binding like the herdr plugin, so status and close are
  available; an existing live pane is reused instead of re-splitting,
  and a reuse with focus re-selects the saved pane
- stamps a per-run ownership marker plus the tmux server PID on the
  pane and on the binding; reuse, status and close verify both, so a
  pane id recycled after a server restart is never killed by mistake -
  a stale pane drops the binding without a kill
- liveness is probed with list-panes, which fails on a gone pane;
  display-message silently returns empty on tmux 3.3+. A pane target
  resolves to its whole window, so the probe formats pane_id into each
  line and reads the binding's own line; any other probe failure
  surfaces as an error instead of a phantom 'gone'
- when focus is not requested the pre-split active pane is re-selected;
  a stamp failure or an abort after the split kills the created pane,
  and the stamp/cleanup pair runs without the signal so cancellation

commit.message:
fix: carry child usage onto workflow step rows (#2723)

* fix: carry child usage onto workflow step rows

A background workflow's parent status kept no token usage or turn
count on its child step rows, so Fleet and the status view showed none,
although each child's own status had them and the workflow total was
their sum. When a workflow child settles, its row now takes the usage
and turn count from the settled result the parent already holds. No new
status reads or watchers.

Related to #2715

* fix: carry usage onto reused workflow child rows

After a runtime reload, relaunching the same workflow reuses a settled
child from the workflow journal or re-attaches to one that is still
running. Both returned before the row update, so those rows still had
no tokens or turn count. The row update now runs where every workflow
child settles (the script host's settle callback), which fresh,
journal-reused and re-attached children all pass through, using the
child results carried on the settled result.

Related to #2715

commit.message:
fix: release Herdr bridge frames after the session adopts the transport (#2710)

BridgeChannel stored every decoded frame and failed the channel after 1,024, so a healthy Herdr-placed run hit the bound and started reconnect handling. Storage is now a pre-adoption backlog: HerdrPiSession adopts the channel on attach and on transport replacement, takes the backlog, and later frames are delivered without being stored. Replay above the evidence cursor still happens before the cursor advances, and an unadopted backlog still fails closed at 1,024 frames. Related to #2706.

commit.message:
perf: keep Fleet's rendered transcript across periodic refreshes (#2709)

The Fleet refresh timer called invalidate() every 750 ms, which dropped the
transcript cache, so an unchanged selected transcript was reread (up to a
2 MiB tail), reparsed and Markdown-rendered on every tick. The timer now
refreshes the roster and requests a render without dropping the cache.
Explicit invalidate() and the refresh key still reread.

The cache fingerprint now also includes the inode and ctime (bigint stat)
so a same-size, same-mtime rewrite is detected, and a failed read (no
events plus a warning) is not cached, so a transient read error recovers
on the next tick.

Related to issue 2705.

commit.message:
fix: compare schedule claim lock file ids exactly on Windows (#2684)

The failed-claim cleanup compared fstat/lstat inode numbers to decide
whether active.lock was still the file this claim created. Windows file
ids are 64-bit with the sequence number in the high bits, so as JS
numbers they lose their low bits and a replacement lock created right
after can compare equal. main CI on 50412418 failed this way in
'keeps a replacement owner's lock when its own claim write fails'.
Use bigint stats so the ids compare exactly.

commit.message:
fix: keep sessions live until child results reach the parent (#2683)

The pi-web liveness provider reported a session idle while a child's
result still owed the parent a handoff: after the async job turned
terminal but before the result watcher handed its result to the
notifier, while a rejected send waited for its retry, and while Pi held
an accepted wake message queued behind the current turn or past
agent_settled. A host replacing idle sessions could drop the result.

The extension now holds each owned top-level terminal job until the
result watcher reports its result delivered, including jobs that a
detached-workflow completion event ends before their status refresh,
and the notifier keeps an accepted wake pending until Pi emits
message_start for it. Both live in memory, are updated at existing
transition points, and are read only when the host asks the existing
provider.

Co-authored-by: brettinternet <20871604+brettinternet@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
fix: serialize schedule history updates across sessions (#2682)

Each session rewrote history.json from its own snapshot, so when two
sessions recorded runs for the same schedule one of the runs could vanish
from the index. Completion matching, restore and delete searched only that
index, so a lost entry left the schedule claimed or made restore drop a
live claim.

Updates to history.json now run under the shared file lease beside it.
Completion, restore and delete read the run's own receipt, which is
written before the lease and is never trimmed. Because the history write
can now time out:
- an unlaunched claim is released when its first records cannot be saved;
- a launched child keeps its claim when its attachment cannot be recorded;
- completion and failed launch release the lock and re-arm the schedule
  before writing history;
- a repeated completion for an old run whose history entry is stale cannot
  release a newer run's claim.

Co-authored-by: quifox <289420841+quifox@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
fix: serialize extension settings updates across sessions (#2680)

* refactor: share the pid-owned file lease with a bounded synchronous wait

Moves the lease from worktree-lock.ts into src/shared/file-lease.ts so
schedule history and extension settings can coordinate short
read-modify-write updates without a second lock implementation or a new
dependency.

* fix: serialize extension settings updates across sessions

Agent override saves, profile application and Watchdog setting changes
each read the settings file, edited it in memory and saved it. Two Pi
sessions doing this at the same time could both read the same snapshot,
and the later save dropped the earlier session's change.

Each of the seven writers now holds the shared file lease beside the
physical settings file (symlinks resolved, so aliases share it) from the
read through the save. Save behavior is unchanged: agent overrides keep
atomic replacement, Profile and Watchdog keep their direct write.

commit.message:
fix: release a schedule claim whose lock file could not be written (#2679)

The launch claim opens active.lock exclusively, then writes the run id.
When that write failed (for example ENOSPC), the descriptor stayed open
and the empty lock remained without an activeRunId, so every later run
of the schedule hit EEXIST and was skipped.

Now the descriptor is checked against the lock path's inode, the lock is
removed only if it is still the file this claim created, the descriptor
is closed, and the original error is rethrown.

Co-authored-by: quifox <289420841+quifox@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
test: keep the slow workflow sibling running until the stop aborts it (#2665)

The sibling-stop tests used a hangUntilAbort mock, which emits agent_end and
agent_settled before it hangs. The child runner treats agent_settled as the end
of the run and, after its 1s final-drain grace, finishes the child as failed
with no output. When the failing sibling and the workflow stop took longer than
that on slow Windows runners, the slow sibling was reported as failed instead
of stopped. A detached runner could also exit early because nothing kept its
event loop alive.

Hold the slow sibling on a release path that never appears instead, so it
emits nothing, its polling keeps the runner process alive, and only the
workflow stop ends it.

Related to #2562

commit.message:
fix: return unfinished streamed text as partial output on timeout or child error (#2653)

* fix: return unfinished streamed text as partial output on timeout or child error

Final output is built from completed message_end messages, so text still streaming when a child timed out or its session threw was lost.

Keep one in-memory reference to the latest unfinished assistant text and return it on timeout or a thrown child-session/prompt error, labeled 'Partial output before timeout:' or 'Partial output before child error:' with outputPartial: true. outputState stays 'present'. The run still fails, the text never satisfies acceptance or a requested output file, and nothing is written to disk. Stop, interrupt, abort, and ordinary non-zero exits are unchanged.

Refs #2549

* fix: clear partial output on completed tool-only replies and defer text extraction

A successful assistant reply that only calls tools now clears the tracked partial text, so a timeout during that tool no longer returns an earlier failed attempt's text as partial output. Stream updates keep only a reference to the latest assistant message; its text is extracted once, when the child ends abnormally. Credit the contributor in the changelog.

Related to #2549

commit.message:
fix: release abandoned workflow capacity slots (#2663)

* fix: release abandoned workflow capacity slots

A terminal workflow kept its active-capacity slot forever when an async child failed without process-terminal proof, because the abandoned-slot policy only covered runner slots. The workflow slot now releases under capacity.abandonedSlotReleaseAfterMs when the workflow ended longer ago than the threshold and every child without proof belongs to the owner session, matches its roster run id and runner identity, and passes the existing failed-run, dead-runner, old-activity rule. Child evidence is read through one shared per-child helper so status proofs and capacity release stay consistent.

Fixes #2658

* fix: keep abandoned slots whose runner PID is in another namespace

A PID recorded in another Linux PID namespace can look dead from this process. Treat that as unknown liveness, as stale-run reconciliation and await-async-run already do.

commit.message:
feat: opt-in command supervision for native Pi children (#2598)

* fix: supervise individual child bash commands

* fix: align command smoke fixtures and custom bash activation

* fix: preserve explicitly required command tool with custom bash

* test: publish service PIDs atomically before cleanup checks

* fix: opt in to native command control and preserve custom tools

* test: await live service abort and Windows fixture cleanup

* fix: retain requested custom-backend command availability

* fix: keep command id metadata within schema token budget

* perf: keep command supervision off status paths

Ordinary targeted status no longer reads command state. It added a
synchronous commands.json read per child, plus a status.json reread for
async runs, on every `{ action: "status", id }`, even for children that
never opted into command supervision. Run state does not record that
opt-in, so command inspection stays with the explicit command.status
action, which the docs already point to.

A read-only command status no longer rewrites commands.json. operate()
persisted on every call with a toolCallId, so the child tool's status
check before and after its wait, and the parent's live command.status,
did full atomic writes when nothing changed. It now persists only when
a yield or cancel changes the command's state.

Also share the header, run, signal, and status lines between the
control notice branches (rendered text unchanged) and drop a delivery
test that repeated the adjacent test and the formatter tests.

* perf: keep the subagent schema within its size budget after merging main

Merging main left SubagentParams at 13,080 serialized chars, over the 13,010 budget. Drop the length bounds on toolCallId (the child-side subagent_command tool takes an unbounded string and the id is only a lookup key) and the gate description's restatement of the object fields its own schema already declares. 13,009 chars.

* docs(schema): say only output json gates produce structuredOutput

* test: keep the gate description wording the schema test asserts

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: launch npm-installed external CLIs on Windows without a shell (#2647)

* fix: launch npm-installed external CLIs on Windows without a shell

npm installs CLIs such as claude, codex, and cursor-agent as .cmd shims.
Since CVE-2024-27980 Node refuses to spawn a .cmd file with shell: false,
so the external-CLI preflight probes and the run spawn failed with EINVAL.

On Windows, resolve the command and, when it is a .cmd that matches npm's
cmd-shim template for a Node bin, run Node (the shim's bundled node.exe
or the resolved Node runtime) on the shim's script with the original
arguments. A command already ending in a PATHEXT extension is looked up
as written, and a batch file found on PATH keeps that path so its target
resolves from the shim's own directory. Every other .cmd or .bat wrapper
is rejected before it runs; no shell is ever used. Native .exe, POSIX,
and status paths are unchanged.

Fixes #2631

* test: use the on-disk shim extension case in the Path lookup assertion

commit.message:
fix: record async runs in run-history.jsonl (parity with foreground executor) (#2620)

* fix: record async runs in run-history.jsonl (parity with foreground executor)

recordRun() was called only by the foreground executor, so every async
launch was invisible to the per-agent run census. With asyncByDefault
that is ALL subagent tool calls on a default install: run-history.jsonl
goes permanently stale (verified on a live machine: last entry 09-23,
140 async launches on 10-01 with zero rows).

Record once at the runner's terminal publication (next to the
subagent.run.completed lifecycle event), mirroring foreground semantics:

- agent: agentName (single agent, or parallel:/chain: composite)
- task: single-step task text via backgroundRunHistoryTask() — feeds
  taskHash, redacted on disk; multi-step runs hash the mode label only,
  never per-step prompts
- exitCode: 0 iff state === "complete" (partial => failed, like the
  result payload's own success field)
- terminal flags: stopped/interrupted/timedOut/first processSignal, so
  paused runs record as "interrupted" like an interrupted foreground run;
  a later resume that settles records again — one entry per attempt

The helper is unit-tested; the wiring itself sits in the 5k-line runner
finalize path which has no existing unit seam, verified end-to-end on a
live machine instead.

* address review: per-step history rows, changelog credit, plan-level tests

- P1: multi-step runs now record one row per child step (agent, own
  durationMs, own exitCode, own processSignal) so loadRunsForAgent(agent)
  sees every child; the composite-only row stayed invisible to per-agent
  lookups. Single-step runs keep the exact foreground shape. Mapping
  extracted into planBackgroundRunHistory(), a pure function.
- P2: planBackgroundRunHistory unit-tested (single/multi/duplicate agents,
  run-level flag propagation, per-step signal, agent-name fallback);
  target file 30/30.
- P0: CHANGELOG Unreleased entry with contributor credit (#2620).

* address review round 2: skip unrun steps, keep finished children's outcomes

- P1 (unrun children count as failures): steps still 'pending' when a run
  ends (e.g. a chain stopped after a failure) get no row — unrun agents
  accumulate no attempts or failures.
- P1 (completed children get wrong outcomes): run-level terminal flags
  (stopped/interrupted/timedOut) now apply only to steps that did not
  reach terminal success; a child that finished before the run was
  interrupted keeps its 'completed' outcome (recordRun lets those flags
  override a successful exit code).
- Both edges unit-tested; pi-coding-agent-dir.test.ts 32/32.

* address review round 3: self-terminal steps keep their own outcome

A step that already reached its own terminal state (completed, failed,
rejected) keeps its own flags instead of inheriting the run-wide
stopped/interrupted/timedOut — otherwise an earlier failure gets
relabeled when a sibling is later interrupted (recordRun() lets those
flags override the exit code). Self-terminal steps now carry their own
timedOut/stopped flags, so a step that timed out itself still records
as timed_out. Run-wide flags apply only to non-self-terminal steps
(running/paused/partial/stopped).

Unit tests added: earlier-failure-not-relabeled, own-timeout-flag;
pi-coding-agent-dir.test.ts 34/34.

* address review round 4: mirror run timeout onto worktree-setup-failed steps

markParallelGroupSetupFailure already set timedOut on the StepResult but
not on the status step, so run-history recorded those agents as plain
'failed' instead of 'timed_out' when a worktree setup timed out. The
step-level flag is the source of truth the history mapper reads.

* record history rows only for children that actually launched

Status alone cannot decide whether a child ran: stopRunner() relabels
pending steps to stopped, timeoutRunner() to failed+timedOut, and
fail-fast and usage-budget skips to failed — all without ever creating
a child session (the fail-fast skip even sets startedAt). The runner
now threads an explicit launched fact per flat index, recorded at the
three dispatch points, and planBackgroundRunHistory() drops
launched:false steps whatever status they were later relabeled to.

Adds runner-level integration tests (runSubagent + fake child sessions
+ temporary PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, reading run-history.jsonl back):
stop queued before a two-step chain starts records zero rows; a
fail-fast parallel run records only the child that ran, not its
skipped sibling; a normally completing chain still records one row per
launched step. Also privatizes backgroundRunHistoryTask per review —
its cases are covered through planBackgroundRunHistory rows.

---------

Co-authored-by: jiaminli <lijiamin411@gmail.com>

commit.message:
feat: let hosts require child extensions for every runner (#2643)

* feat: let hosts require child extensions for every runner

registerRequiredChildExtensions gains requireForAllRunners. When set,
the host's required extensions become mandatory for every launch rather
than being excluded on routes that cannot load them. Only a local native
Pi child loads these extensions, so a launch that resolves to an external
CLI runner, an external-job runner, or any machine placement is rejected
before a runner process is spawned, a provider job starts, or a task is
handed off. The flag is stamped onto each snapshot entry so it survives
the nested, detached, resumed, recovered, and appended carriers, and a
disposed registration or an extensions: [] override cannot drop it.
Existing registrations without the flag keep excluding external runners.

Related to #2639

* fix: write the retained extension snapshot without an extra parent-session read

The chain launch read ctx.parentSessionId once more before building its
steps, so a launch whose parent identity changed between reads was no
longer rejected as inconsistent. Write the snapshot after the launch
parent is resolved and reuse that value.

Related to #2639

* fix: name required extension IDs when a foreground machine launch is refused

A foreground native launch with machine placement was already refused
before remote work by the remote serializer, but with a generic message.
Run the shared admission check there so the error names the required
extension IDs. Also state exactly what preflight previews.

Related to #2639

commit.message:
fix: reject a child whose required extension fails during startup (#2640)

* fix: reject a child whose required extension fails during startup

Pi reports session_start handler errors through the extension error
callback instead of throwing, so a host-required extension that failed
to initialize still produced a usable child. Errors attributed to a
required extension during bindExtensions now dispose the child and
reject the launch. Ordinary extension errors are unchanged.

Related to #2639

* fix: run session_shutdown before rejecting a required startup failure

Binding finishes before the required failure is acted on, so the other
extensions' session_start handlers have already run and may hold
watchers or servers. Reuse the factory's shutdown sequence instead of a
bare dispose.

Related to #2639

commit.message:
fix: verify virtual-model children against their selection, not the dispatched model (#2638)

* fix: verify virtual-model children against their selection, not the dispatched model

Pi 1.0.0 records a virtual-model turn in two places: the selection
(session.model, model_change entries) names the virtual model, and the
assistant message names the physical model the router dispatched to.
Both verification call sites compared the launch model with the
assistant message's model, so a child launched on router/auto failed
with model_verification_failed even when it ran correctly.

The local child-session adapter now exposes virtualModelId, the live
provider/id of the selected model when Pi marks it with
api === "pi-virtual". When that is present, the verifier compares it
exactly with the launch model (without its thinking suffix) and skips
the physical-model check. A different virtual selection still fails.
Without the marker, and for remote Herdr children, verification is
unchanged. Displayed and recorded physical model ids are unchanged.

Fixes #2637

* fix: give virtual-model verification failures their own message

The alias advice in the shared failure text cannot fix a virtual-model
selection mismatch. Document virtual-model verification next to
modelResponseAliases.

commit.message:
fix: flush queued virtual model registrations in child sessions (#2636)

* fix: flush queued virtual model registrations in child sessions

Pi core queues pendingVirtualModelRegistrations during extension loading
and flushes them when a session binds extensions (agent-session-services).
The child session factory resolves the requested model before
bindExtensions, so an extension-registered virtual model was never in the
registry at resolution time: 'provider/virtual-id' fell through pi's
OpenRouter-style full-string fallback and the child died on provider auth
(e.g. 'No API key found for openrouter').

Flush the queue in flushQueuedProviderRegistrations, next to the provider
and native provider queues. The structural casts keep compiling against
SDK versions that predate virtual models; there the queue is absent and
the loop is a no-op. Virtual models do not claim provider ids, so parent
provider inheritance is unchanged.

Verified end to end against pi 0.99.2 with a Jev-classifier virtual model
as subagents.defaultModel: children now resolve and dispatch through the
router (standard/complex tiers observed on both dispatch targets).

* docs: credit the child virtual-model registration fix in the changelog

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

commit.message:
feat: let the Claude Code adapters take a model and a thinking level (#2603)

The code-owned claude-code and claude-code-writer adapters own their argv, so a
launch could not choose a Claude model. A per-call model was refused, a per-call
thinking level was dropped, frontmatter model and thinking were rejected as
Pi-only fields, and the adapters' own commandPrefixArgs hook was never populated
by the launch path.

The existing paths do not express a per-launch choice. Claude Code user settings
are global to every run of the CLI, and a wrapper executable has to be written
and then kept in sync while it replaces the fixed argv the adapter exists to own.

Take the model and the level in the form dispatch already has for Pi children:

- The level travels as the `:level` suffix on `model`, so
  `model: "claude-opus-5.5:high"` pins both and `model: ":high"` sets the level on
  the agent's own model. A suffix wins over the frontmatter thinking value.
- resolveClaudeCodeOverride splits the suffix before validating, maps the level
  onto --effort (off passes no flag, minimal maps to low), and rejects an unusable
  model or level by name. The tokens are appended after the fixed argv, so the
  --version and --help probes never see them.
- An explicit `thinking: false` clears the level instead of falling back to the
  agent's own value, which would have applied the level the caller just cleared.
- subagents.maxThinking applies: a request above the ceiling fails before the
  child starts, compared on the requested level rather than the effort it maps to.
- An enforced subagents.modelScope covers these launches too, checked against the
  model id that will reach the CLI, and a launch that pins no model fails closed,
  because the CLI's own default cannot be checked.
- subagents.defaultModel is a default for Pi children and never becomes --model. A
  per-launch or frontmatter model is passed on as given.
- A pinned model on a saved machine is refused instead of losing both flags, and
  preflight reports the same failures as the launch under a new model_scope code.

The dispatch contract is asserted twice. test/unit/claude-code-dispatch.test.ts
builds the steps with buildAsyncRunnerSteps and feeds them to the launch, and
test/integration/claude-code-dispatch.test.ts runs the real runner against a fake
claude that records its argv. The launch file is skipped on Windows because the
adapter spawns its command with shell: false, and Node refuses to spawn a .cmd
file that way, so the same contract is covered on every platform by the unit file
and by the real Node spawn in claude-code-adapter.test.ts.

Only these two adapters accept the override. codex-exec, cursor-agent and
external-job keep refusing model and thinking, and the machine rejection only
covers the Claude Code adapters.

docs/agents.md, docs/models.md, docs/tool-reference.md, docs/extension-api.md and
CHANGELOG.md carry the contract.

  onto --effort (off passes no flag, minimal maps to low), and rejects an unusable
  model or level by name. The tokens are appended after the fixed argv, so the
  --version and --help probes never see them.
- An explicit `thinking: false` clears the level instead of falling back to the
  agent's own value, which would have applied the level the caller just cleared.
- subagents.maxThinking applies: a request above the ceiling fails before the
  child starts, compared on the requested level rather than the effort it maps to.
- An enforced subagents.modelScope covers these launches too, checked against the
  model id that will reach the CLI, and a launch that pins no model fails closed,
  because the CLI's own default cannot be checked.
- subagents.defaultModel is a default for Pi children and never becomes --model. A
  per-launch or frontmatter model is passed on as given.
- A pinned model on a saved machine is refused instead of losing both flags, and
  preflight reports the same failures as the launch under a new model_scope code.

The dispatch contract is asserted twice. test/unit/claude-code-dispatch.test.ts
builds the steps with buildAsyncRunnerSteps and feeds them to the launch, and
test/integration/claude-code-dispatch.test.ts runs the real runner against a fake
claude that records its argv. The launch file is skipped on Windows because the
adapter spawns its command with shell: false, and Node refuses to spawn a .cmd
file that way, so the same contract is covered on every platform by the unit file
and by the real Node spawn in claude-code-adapter.test.ts.

Only these two adapters accept the override. codex-exec, cursor-agent and
external-job keep refusing model and thinking, and the machine rejection only
covers the Claude Code adapters.

docs/agents.md, docs/models.md, docs/tool-reference.md, docs/extension-api.md and
CHANGELOG.md carry the contract.

A legacy `expand` dynamic-fanout step whose parallel template used an

status steps now carry the external runner status like static parallel
children, so status, fleet view, and retained-child handling treat them
as external.

commit.message:
fix: stop /subagent-cost logging missing workflow receipts and mark them unavailable (#2615)

* fix: stop cost collection reading receipts for foreground workflows

Every /subagent-cost or RPC cost call logged "Workflow receipt '<id>' was
not found." once per foreground workflow in the session. Cost collection
queued every workflow result's runId for a receipt lookup, but only async
workflows write a receipt file; a foreground workflow keeps its receipt
inline and already reports child usage in its results. The ENOENT guard
around the lookup never matched because readWorkflowReceipt rethrows the
missing-file case as a plain Error.

Only queue workflow results that carry an asyncId, which every async
workflow launch result has. Unreadable async receipts are still logged.
Fixes #2614.

* fix: report async workflows without a receipt as unavailable in cost

An async workflow with no receipt yet, such as one still running, made
every /subagent-cost or RPC cost call log "Workflow receipt '<id>' is not
available ..." and left that workflow's children out of the totals with
no "Async child usage unavailable" line. readWorkflowReceipt rethrew the
missing-file case as a plain Error, so the collector's ENOENT check never
matched, and its catch did not count the workflow as unresolved.

readWorkflowReceipt now keeps the original ENOENT as the error's cause,
with unchanged messages. Cost collection skips logging when the receipt
is missing and counts a workflow it cannot resolve as unavailable, unless
a bg_wait completion already reported its children. Unreadable receipts
are still logged. Refs #2614.

* fix: mark a workflow without a readable receipt unavailable even after a bg_wait completion

commit.message:
fix: count every resumed foreground workflow round in /subagent-cost (#2612)

Resuming a foreground workflow child appends each round to the same child
session file. Foreground workflow results carried no run id, so
collectSubagentCost keyed them by session file and dropped every round after
the first as a duplicate. /subagent-cost and the RPC cost method then
under-reported spend without any warning.

Foreground workflow results now carry the child's run id. This is the same id
that workflow receipt continuation lineages use, so each round is keyed as
run:<runId> and counted once. A result replayed in a slash-result message is
still counted once.

Fixes #2601.

commit.message:
fix: treat workflow "true" from MCP clients as workflow: true (#2610)

* fix: treat workflow "true" from MCP clients as workflow: true

Some MCP clients, such as pi-claude-bridge, send the boolean branch of the
subagent workflow union as the string "true". The tool then looked up a
workflow resource named "true" and failed with an error advising
workflow: true, which the caller had already sent, so a retry could never
succeed.

Public execution normalization now coerces workflow "true" to true before
any branching, so execute, validate, async, and schedule.create all read the
reply's js workflow block and a resource or file named "true" can never be
resolved. The one-call-per-reply count also counts the string form. Other
string coercions and the schema are unchanged.

Refs #2600

* fix: reject workflow "true" at the RPC spawn boundary like workflow: true

commit.message:
fix: notify attention for each long-open tool call (#2613)

* fix: notify attention for each long-open tool call

A child that kept a second tool call open past the attention threshold
never notified the parent. The notification key ignored the tool call
id, so two long-open bash calls with the same context collided, and the
foreground and background producers skipped open-tool attention while the
child was already in needs_attention.

Track attention per active tool call, pass its toolCallId on the control
event, include that id in the notification key for tool_open_threshold
events, and drop the needs_attention gate for open-tool attention. Each
distinct call now notifies once, and the same call still notifies only
once. Anonymous calls do not report a toolCallId.

Split from #2598.

Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

* fix: keep attention when a supervisor request ends before a long tool call

A background child could lose needs_attention while a long-open tool call
was still running. When a supervisor request was open, the runner saved
the earlier activity state so it could restore it when the request ended.
Open-tool attention now fires during that request and marks the call as
notified, so when the supervisor tool ended first the restore dropped
needs_attention and the still-open call never set it again.

When open-tool attention fires for a step with a saved supervisor state,
update the saved state to needs_attention so the restore keeps it.

* test: wait for supervisor cleanup before checking attention state

---------

Co-authored-by: jiuai233 <252142369@qq.com>

commit.message:
fix: match Pi's built-in MCP names for hyphenated mcp: selectors (#2607) (#2609)

With Pi's built-in MCP, a selector such as mcp:srv/get-item failed parent
preflight with "selects MCP tools that Pi's built-in MCP does not offer".
Pi's createMcpToolName replaces everything but [A-Za-z0-9_] with _, and
mcpNamespace replaces - with _, so the tool registers as mcp__srv__get_item
in namespace mcp__srv. The parent kept the -, so it never found the tool or,
for a hyphenated server, its namespace. The parent now sanitizes the same
way. The child already grants by the raw <server>/<tool> label, so the raw
selector works end to end and stays the one documented form.

commit.message:
fix(workflows): show a revived workflow child as its key's latest run (#2585)

* fix(workflows): show a revived workflow child as its key's latest run

A failed async workflow child revived with a top-level resume ran as a detached run that nothing linked back to its workflow key, so the workflow's status, receipt, and keyed latest:true resume kept pointing at the failure. The revive now writes a link in the failed source run's directory (and an origin copy in the revived run's directory). Workflow status, keyed resume, and terminal publication follow those links by exact reads: receipts and keyed resume append the revived run to the key's lineage, and status and completion notices show the revival's state next to the original failure, which is kept unchanged. Only failed sources are linked, and chains are capped at 16 when recorded.

Fixes #2579

* fix(workflows): keep revived runs from retention and report unreadable source status

A revived workflow child has no workflow owner in its status, so async retention could delete it and cut its key's revival chain; its origin record now marks it as a workflow reference. Recording a revival no longer hides a source status read error; it shows on the revive receipt as the existing link warning.

* fix(workflows): drop the origin record when the revival link cannot be written

* fix(workflows): keep the origin record when the revival link was published

A write can publish its file and still throw while removing its temporary file. Remove the origin record only when the source's link does not name this revival, so a published chain stays protected from retention.

commit.message:
fix(tui): count running agents the same way in the async widget and Fleet view (#2584)

The progressive widget header counted running root jobs while the Fleet view counts active leaf agents, so a 4-lane workflow next to one other run read "2 agents running" beside "5 active agents". The header now counts per running job what collectFleetStatusEntries counts: a workflow counts its loaded child runs, other jobs count their active steps, synthesized from agents when a job has no step detail.

Fixes #2578

commit.message:
fix(tui): show lanes instead of blank rows in the progressive async widget (#2583)

* fix(tui): show lanes instead of blank rows in the progressive async widget

The progressive async-widget tier locked the card to the compact cap and
padded it with blank rows, showing one line per root job, so a workflow's
lanes stayed hidden. Fill the rows left after the visible job lines with
the visible workflows' lane rows, and lock the card height to the rows the
content fills at lock time. The height stays fixed between relocks.

Fixes #2578

* fix(tui): grow the content-sized progressive card when jobs start

A progressive card locked to its content (for example two rows for one
job) had no room for a job that started before the next relock: the only
body row became the +N more line and the job details disappeared. When
jobs are hidden and the lock is below the compact cap, grow the lock to
the rows the content needs, up to the cap. The lock never shrinks between
relocks, so finishing jobs keep the fixed height.

commit.message:
fix(schema): anchor the acceptance JSON-string pattern for llama.cpp (#2582)

llama.cpp builds a grammar from each tool schema and rejects patterns that are not anchored with both ^ and $, so every request with the subagent tool registered failed with a 400. ^\s*\{[\s\S]*$ matches the same strings as the old ^\s*\{. A schema walk now rejects any unanchored pattern.

Fixes #2581

commit.message:
feat(mcp): support Pi built-in MCP for mcp: tool selections (#2573)

* feat(mcp): resolve mcp: selectors against Pi built-in MCP in the parent

* feat(mcp): load Pi built-in MCP for selected tools in child sessions

* feat(mcp): support Pi built-in MCP for mcp: tool selections

Connect the parent resolver and the child runtime for foreground and
background children. The parent's built-in resolution travels to the
async runner in the step, so the runner no longer falls back to adapter
resolution, and background children get MCP_DIRECT_TOOLS=__none__.
Foreground launches that select a server only an extension registered
fail in the parent with a message pointing at async: true. The child's
MCP readiness wait now runs after the launch lock is released, so it no
longer delays other child launches. Preflight accepts the host so it
resolves built-in selectors too.

* fix(mcp): shut down a child still waiting for MCP tools when the factory is disposed

factory.dispose() did not know about a child in its MCP readiness wait,
so the child could open after dispose. Dispose now ends the wait, shuts
the session down and waits for it, and create rejects.

* refactor(mcp): skip mcp.json reads for foreground launches without extension servers

Check the selected servers against pi.getMcpServers() before reading
any mcp.json, inline the one-line /mcp owner check, and document that
preflight without runtimeSnapshotHost resolves mcp: selections through
pi-mcp-adapter's configuration. Docs note that a child reads the
project's .pi/mcp.json only when the parent trusts the project.

* fix(mcp): hide unselected built-in MCP tools in child sessions

The child's MCP wrapper now registers every tool it does not grant as
hidden, so codemode and ctx.executeTool() cannot reach it even without
the child's tools allowlist, which already keeps those tools out today.

* fix(mcp): skip an untrusted project's .pi/mcp.json in the foreground check

The foreground check for extension-registered servers now reads the
project's .pi/mcp.json only when the launch trusts the project, as Pi's
own MCP config loader does, and its error names the files that count.

* fix(mcp): grant a mcp:server/tool selection only to the raw tool it names

Pi gives the sanitized name of a raw MCP tool to whichever tool
registers first and a hash suffix to a colliding one, so mcp:srv/a.b
resolved to the name of srv/a_b. The parent now prefers the
hash-suffixed name Pi derives from the raw server and tool, and the
child exposes a granted name only when the tool's <server>/<tool> label
matches the selector that granted it, failing the launch otherwise.
The runner step carries each granted name with its selector.

commit.message:
fix(skills): drop extension skills when inheritSkills is false (#2541)

With inheritSkills: false, skills from extensions loaded into an in-process child still reached the child's prompt. Pi applies noSkills only to the initial skill set, and extendResources later merges resources_discover skill paths without checking it. The child loader now also passes skillsOverride returning no skills when noSkills is set; Pi applies it on every skills update. Herdr-placed children still rely on Pi's --no-skills.

Fixes #2540

commit.message:
feat(model-scope): add scoped allow token for Pi's scoped models (#2538)

subagents.modelScope allow lists accept a reserved scoped token. At each child launch it expands in the parent to the parent session's scoped models (Pi's /scoped-models), so subagent restrictions follow Pi's model scoping without a second copy of the list. Every launch path passes the scoped-model snapshot; background runs keep the set captured at start. When the parent session is unscoped, scoped means the same as inherit, which is narrower than Pi's unscoped behavior. An enforced scoped entry with no parent model fails closed like inherit. Violation messages list at most 8 patterns.

Co-authored-by: Corey Ryan Hanson <17171838+coreyryanhanson@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
fix(retention): reclaim async runs bound to terminal or pruned missions (#2536)

Async run retention kept every run with a mission binding forever, so old runs accumulated once their mission finished or was pruned. Retention now reclaims old runs whose mission is terminal or no longer exists. It keeps runs whose mission is still active, whose binding or mission record cannot be read, and runs with a pending mission observer index, because the watcher needs the run's binding to retry that mission sync.

Fixes #2535

commit.message:
fix(activation): let the model check its tool list after subagents_enable (#2525)

The subagents_enable result told the model that on some providers
subagent appears only after the next user prompt, so it should not retry
it in this turn. pi-subagents cannot tell which provider is running, so
on native Pi providers, and on bridges that refresh the tool list
mid-turn, the model was told to wait even though subagent was already
available.

The result now tells the model to check its own tool list: if a subagent
tool is there (possibly with a prefix), call it, starting with
list+capabilities; if not, the provider fixes the tool list for the
whole prompt, so wait for the next user prompt instead of retrying. The
--exclude-tools subagents_enable operator hint and the appended
advertised catalog are unchanged.

commit.message:
fix(async): scope runner liveness probes to the PID namespace (#2498)

Stale-run reconciliation no longer marks a live async run failed when a Pi process in a different PID namespace (another container, or a macOS/Windows host sharing a container's PI_SUBAGENTS_TEMP_ROOT) probes its PID and gets ESRCH. Runs record their Linux PID namespace; a probe that cannot match it falls back to the existing 24-hour stale-status rule.

Related to #2494 and #2495.

commit.message:
feat: support external inspector registration (#2482)

Loaded extensions can register external inspector providers through the pi-subagents:inspector-register:v1 event or the pi-subagents/inspectors helper. Fleet and inspector actions use them after the built-in Herdr and Ghostty inspectors. Registrations are shared by the pi-subagents runtimes on the Pi event bus, so they survive a duplicate-runtime takeover, and are cleared when the last runtime shuts down.

commit.message:
test(nested-control): wait for runner terminal proof and keep its cwd out of the fixture (#2470)

* test(nested-control): wait for runner terminal proof before cleanup

A complete run is not proof that its runner exited, and signal-zero on the status pid can remain positive on Windows after an identity-matched runner close was observed. Use the persisted process-terminal proof to finish the test, and avoid spawning the runner with a disposable fixture directory as cwd. Keep cleanup errors visible instead of relying on an unproven longer retry.

* test(nested-control): record the source run cwd outside the fixture

A follow-up runner starts in the source run's recorded cwd, not the
caller's, so passing ctx(os.tmpdir()) did not move it. Record the
isolated test root as the nested run's cwd instead.

commit.message:
fix(external-job): follow up child-launched external-job runs (#2466)

* fix(external-job): follow up child-launched external-job runs

A session resolves the runs of its children as nested runs, and the
nested resume path always needs a Pi session file. An external-job run
has none. So resume from a child failed with "does not have a persisted
session file to resume from", and the provider's followUp never ran.
Only root-launched async runs reached the external-job follow-up path.

When the selected step of a nested run has an external-job runner, the
resume target now comes from the run's own directory, built with
resolveAsyncResumeTarget and nestedRunScope. The existing follow-up
gates then apply, and a live run gets the existing "still running"
message. A launch status has no runner yet. If the agent definition is
external-job, the resume fails closed with the existing "no persisted
provider metadata" message. Nested Pi runs with a session file keep
session-file revival.

A child launches the follow-up under its nested route, so the duplicate
check now looks there too. Before, a repeated resume from a child called
the provider's followUp a second time.

* fix(external-job): surface agent discovery errors on nested resume

A launch-status nested run looked up its agent definition to decide
whether it was an external-job run, but swallowed discovery failures
and fell back to the Pi session-file error. Let the discovery error
reach the caller instead.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(external-job): service bridges of child-launched runs (#2450)

* fix(external-job): service bridges of child-launched runs

Only the root session's async job tracker serviced external-job bridge
requests. A child session's fanout subagent tool launched async runs but
never serviced their bridges, so an external-job agent launched by a child
stayed queued. A child session now services the bridges of the
external-job runs it launches.

Closes #2449

* fix(external-job): keep child runs tracked until runner metadata settles

async-execution writes the launch status.json before the runner starts.
Its steps carry only agent and status, with no runner field, and the
subagent:async-started event fires at that point. The runner adds the
runner metadata later. externalJobBridgeEligibility reads an omitted
runner as not-required, so the child sweeper deleted the run when it
swept before the runner wrote its status. The runner then wrote its
bridge request, and nothing serviced it.

The child sweeper now keeps every run until the run is final, as the
root tracker does. It skips servicing on sweeps where the status says
no bridge is required, and re-checks on the next sweep.

Refs #2449

commit.message:
fix(worktree): keep UTF-8 naming labels within byte cap (#2447)

* fix(worktree): keep naming labels within byte cap when truncation splits multi-byte UTF-8

truncateUtf8 cut the encoded buffer at exactly maxBytes and decoded the
dangling bytes to U+FFFD (3 bytes each), so a label truncated at a
multi-byte boundary could exceed the 256-byte naming-label cap. The

commit.message:
fix(agents): honor hidden skill model invocation (#2412)

* fix(agents): respect disable-model-invocation when injecting subagent skills

Skills marked `disable-model-invocation: true` are meant to be user-only:
invocable via explicit `/skill:name` commands but excluded from the model-
facing skill set. pi-subagents' skill loader parsed only `name`/`description`
and never read that flag, so any broad skill list resolved for a child could
leak hidden skills into the subagent's `<available_skills>` prompt.

Parse `disable-model-invocation` from skill frontmatter (matching the pi
host's loader semantics: only the literal string "true" opts out) and thread
it through discovery and resolution as `disableModelInvocation`. Filter on it
in `buildSkillInjection` — the single chokepoint every prompt-injection path
funnels through — so hidden skills never reach a child prompt regardless of
which caller assembled the list.

Explicitly naming a hidden skill still resolves it (it stays user-invocable),
but it is dropped at injection time, aligning with the "hidden = user-only"
contract.

Add test/unit/skills-disable-model-invocation.test.ts covering metadata
exposure, explicit-name resolution, buildSkillInjection filtering (including
the all-hidden empty case), the pushEntry priority-upgrade branch, and
non-"true" flag values.

* fix(agents): honor disable-model-invocation in proactive skill recommendations

Greptile review follow-ups for #2400:

- recommendProactiveSkillSubagents drops hidden skills (and their
  descriptions) from model-facing proactive recommendations; the
  AvailableSkill type now carries disableModelInvocation.
- Fix the priority-upgrade test to actually exercise pushEntry's same-file
  branch: register the shared skill dir via a settings entry, then a
  same-target symlink, so the second pass hits the same resolved file at
  higher project priority.
- Add a recommendation test pinning that hidden skills are not suggested.
- Credit @toRolex in the Unreleased changelog, per repo policy.

* test(agents): cover name-level source precedence for disableModelInvocation

The previous test claimed to exercise pushEntry's same-file priority-upgrade
branch, but pushEntry keys its seen map by path.resolve (lexical), and the
.pi/skills root scan lexically covers any .pi-relative settings path — so that
branch never actually ran. Replace it with a test over the path that is
reachable in practice: two same-named skills from different sources, where
name-level dedup (chooseHigherPrioritySkill) keeps the higher-priority project
entry and that entry must carry the flag. Verified by mutation: disabling the
flag read in readSkill, or breaking the higher-priority-wins dedup, both turn
the test red.

Also drop the now-unused makeProjectPackageSkill helper.

* fix(skills): match host YAML boolean semantics

---------

Co-authored-by: rolex <torolex@163.com>

commit.message:
fix: detect dynamic tool support from the running Pi installation (#2398)

* fix: detect dynamic tool support from the running Pi installation

The host SDK is not a dependency of this package, so a bare module
resolution only succeeds where it happens to be installed next to us — a
repository checkout with devDependencies. Every distributed install (npm or
git) resolved nothing, warned, and silently kept the subagent tool eager:
the compact subagents_enable loader never appeared, even on hosts that
support it.

Read the version from the running host instead, using the same root
precedence as host-owned child sessions (running host, explicit override,
install tree). The 0.86.1 floor is unchanged, and a missing host package now
reports that it could not verify support instead of claiming the host is too
old.

Closes #2397.

* fix: keep host manifest failures visible while gating dynamic tools

Review feedback on the first revision: the probe collapsed every read or
parse failure into undefined, so a selected root with a broken manifest was
silently replaced by a different Pi installation, and the caller could only
report a generic "could not locate" warning.

The selected root is now authoritative — running host, then an explicit
override, then the install tree, the precedence host-owned child sessions
already use — and its concrete manifest failure, missing version, or
foreign package identity is reported as the reason. The version floor
message also names the installation it measured, so a decision made from an
unconfirmed root cannot look like it came from the running host.

* fix: fail closed when the running Pi host cannot be verified

The activation gate only trusts the Pi that owns the session: the running
host, or an explicit PI_SUBAGENTS_PI_CODING_AGENT_PACKAGE_ROOT override. An
SDK reachable through our own install tree cannot be proven to be that
installation, so it no longer decides the version floor — dynamic
activation stays off, and the reason names the unconfirmed root.

Tests that exercise activation now declare the host they simulate instead of
relying on a copy next to the checkout.
