commit.message:
fix(agents): apply model settings to runtime-registered agents (#2369)

* fix(agents): apply subagent model settings to runtime-registered agents

Runtime-registered agents were appended to discovery after every settings
pass, so `subagents.defaultModel`, `defaultProvider`, `defaultThinking`, and
`agentOverrides.<name>` never reached them and they silently inherited the
parent session model while `/subagents-models` reported the same.

`mergeRuntimeAgents` now takes the discovery context (cwd, scope, preferred
provider) and runs runtime agents through the existing default/override
pipeline. Only the model-tier override fields (`model`, `defaultProvider`,
`fast`, `thinking`) apply; prompt, tools, context, and every other field stay
owned by the registering extension. A definition `model` still wins over
`defaultModel`, and `model: false` returns the agent to session inheritance.

* Update CHANGELOG.md

commit.message:
fix(child-session): preserve host SDK ownership (#2352)

* test(pi-spawn): cover host package root discovery from installed entries

* fix(child-session): load the host SDK from the resolved host package root

The default in-process child session factory imported
@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent through a bare specifier, which resolves
against the extension's own node_modules tree. On npm-hosted Pi
installations the peer packages live outside that tree, and Pi 0.86.0 no
longer serves virtual module resolution to extension code, so foreground
child launches failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND while the host itself ran
fine.

Resolve the host package root (PI_SUBAGENTS_PI_CODING_AGENT_PACKAGE_ROOT
override, then pi-subagents' install location, then the running pi
binary's location) and import the host's entry file by file URL, so
children share the host's single SDK instance. A bare import remains the
last resort; an explicitly overridden root that cannot be imported is
reported instead of masked.

* fix(child-session): prefer the running host root, validate root identity, preserve host errors

Address review findings on the host-SDK loader:

- Prefer the running pi process's location over the package manager's view
  of pi-subagents' install tree, matching how the existing child-launch
  code treats installed-package resolution as the last fallback. An
  extension tree that contains its own (stale) pi-coding-agent copy no
  longer shadows the host that owns the child.
- Validate package.json identity before importing a selected root, as the
  documented override contract promises: roots naming another package are
  rejected with a configuration error instead of executing unrelated code.
- Stop masking host SDK failures: only module-resolution failures on an
  auto-discovered root fall through to the bare specifier; evaluation and
  dependency errors from a correctly discovered host are reported as-is.

* test(child-session): cover override identity rejection and Windows symlink portability

- Rejecting an override root whose package.json name is not
  @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent now has direct coverage.
- The bin-symlink discovery test skips on Windows, where file symlinks
  require elevated privileges, matching the established test pattern.

* fix(child-session): preserve host SDK ownership

---------

Co-authored-by: nazerim <nazerim@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
fix(runner): settle aborted runs whose session creation hangs

abortChild returned early when no session existed yet, so it never armed
the ABORT_SETTLE_MS backstop. A hung factory.create() therefore ignored
the run timeout, stop and interrupt indefinitely, and because session
opens are serialized process-wide, one wedged extension startup left the
run "running" until the 24h stale-run threshold.

Abort the session only when one exists and always arm the settle timer.
A session that arrives after the forced settle is already disposed by
the launch block.

chore(release): v0.69.0

Typed gates with JSON verdicts, Ghostty detection fix for embedding terminals, and quiet startup without npm.

feat(acceptance): typed gates bridge json stdout into structuredOutput (#2315)

* feat(acceptance): typed gates bridge json stdout into structuredOutput

`gate` now accepts `{ command, output: "json", schema?, timeoutMs? }` in
addition to the string form. When a typed gate passes, its stdout is parsed
(and validated against `schema` when given) and becomes the child's
`structuredOutput`, recorded on the verify run and projected into
status.json. Empty, truncated, non-JSON, or schema-invalid stdout fails the
gate so the verdict is never dropped silently. Typed gates are never
memoized, because their inputs (a report, a log) can change without the
tracked tree changing, and `output: "json"` rejects `outputSchema` so a run
has one structured-output source.

This lets a post-run classifier supply a verdict that `runs.lanes` and
workflow scripts branch on without the parent reading the child's output.
Docs cover the gate contract and command-runner agents as typed workflow
steps; `examples/typed-gate` is a runnable, vendor-free version of both.

Also corrects the tool reference: `maxOutput` has no default cap.

* fix(acceptance): reject explicit typed verify commands combined with outputSchema

The gate shorthand already rejected output: "json" alongside outputSchema,
but the same policy written as an explicit acceptance.verify entry slipped
through and the agent's structured_output silently won over the gate value.
Both spellings normalize to the same verify commands, so preflight now checks
the normalized policy once and names which spelling conflicted.

* fix(acceptance): keep one structured-output source across every spelling

Greptile pointed out that an agent-declared outputSchema could still coexist
with a typed gate. The check now runs once after agent defaults are merged,
where the effective outputSchema (launch param or frontmatter) and the
effective acceptance (gate, explicit verify list, or defaultAcceptance) are
both known, and the error names both sources. Documented in the tool
reference, changelog, and the bundled pi-subagents skill, which also gains a
note on typed gates and command-runner agents as typed steps.

commit.message: fix(delegation): require exact budget block message
fix(delegation): report blocked tool budgets

fix: keep detached workflow work visible and accurately reported

Preserve explicit async dispatch without treating launch receipts as completed child work or final report references. Retain session-owned nested routing after coordinator cleanup and prevent mission-only directories from shadowing real runs.

fix(orca-progress-tabs): keep the viewer one-liner free of backslashes

Orca runs `terminal create --command` through the user's login shell, while the
viewer one-liner is quoted as a POSIX single-quoted string. fish collapses `\\`
inside single quotes to `\`, so `node -e` received `char==='\'` — an unterminated
string literal — and every progress tab opened on a SyntaxError instead of the
progress mirror.

Comparing against `String.fromCharCode(92)` removes the only two backslashes from
the viewer script, so the same quoted command round-trips through POSIX shells and
fish alike. The `'"'"'` quoting idiom is unchanged, and the regression test asserts
the generated command carries no backslash.
